does: Encloses a filling or a piece of food in a wrapper, such as caul fat, a leaf, a thin omelette or a cloth, and closes it by folding or pulling, so that it keeps its shape and its juices as it cooks.

intro.what: Wrapping encloses food in a flexible leaf, sheet or other covering and secures the seam.
intro.why: It teaches you to leave a useful border and balance a snug closure with room for the filling.

how: Lay the wrapper out flat and make sure it is soft enough to bend without tearing.
Set the food or the filling in the middle, with a border all round.
Fold the sides over the food, then bring the ends in and over, so that the wrapper meets itself and overlaps a little.
Turn the parcel seam side down, or tie it, so that it stays closed in the heat.

cues.text: The wrapper lies snugly round the food, with the seam underneath and no gaps.
The parcel is firm and holds its shape when it is lifted.

mistakes.mistake: Overfilling, so that the wrapper splits when the filling swells.
mistakes.fix: Use less filling and leave a border.

mistakes.mistake: Wrapping loosely, so that the parcel falls open in the pan.
mistakes.fix: Pull the wrapper snug and set it seam side down, or tie it.

quiz.question: Why leave a border around the filling?
choices: To leave the filling exposed at every side.
To allow the wrapper to overlap and close.
To make the wrapper stretch as thin as possible.
quiz.because: The clear border supplies material for a complete enclosure instead of an overfilled seam.

quiz.question: How should the finished parcel be secured?
choices: Leave the seam loose on top.
Fold the ends without letting the wrapper edges overlap.
Set it seam down or tie it.
quiz.because: An underside seam or tie helps the overlapping wrapper stay in place.

quiz.question: Which appearance fits a neatly wrapped parcel?
choices: A snug covering with no gaps and the seam underneath.
A loose covering with exposed filling.
Torn corners around an overfilled centre.
quiz.because: A complete covering supports the shape without open routes for filling to escape.

quiz.question: The wrapper split as the filling expanded. What would you change next time?
choices: Stretch the next wrapper tighter over more filling.
Use less filling and leave a border.
Remove the overlap to fit extra filling.
quiz.because: A smaller filling and enough wrapper reduce strain while keeping the enclosure complete.
